content:
Hi!

I am currently writing a custom tactic for simplifying goals involving do notation inside Monads with effects like LawfulMonadStateOf. It started out with the tactic just being a simp_all [...] with a lot of added theorems such as LawfulMonadStateOf.modifyGet_eq. Initially this worked quite well, but for a bit more involved proofs it's already getting really really slow.

Do you have any advice how I could speedup the tactic? Maybe adding more higher level theorems for simplifying the goals? Switching away from simp_all entirely? Thanks!
In general you probably want to use mvcgen instead of rolling your own reasoning engine about do notation.

I'm having some issues with mvcgen. For me personally, it fails to generate anything all the time. One of my usecases is proving the equivalance of two do blocks. I first simplify them using simp_all [...] and then use tactics like congr to prove for example that the final state is the same. How would I do this using mvcgen?
Can you post an #mwe of an example where mvcgen fails to generate anything?
It's a bit of an involved project, so it will take me some time to setup an MWE. I will attempt it though.
